properties.role: Tide-reader who rows boats near the bell water
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her, never meets anyone's eye and keeps her gaze on the tide line; blunt, shrugs and returns to her net.
properties.wants: Never to be out on the water at night; will row the party by day.
properties.knows: Her grandmother said the water in Saltmere came up warm the night it flooded.

sources.quote: She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net.

changes.why: She works the docks at pier four.

change.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Saltmere Mine flooded forty years ago on the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Links the mine to the bell's origin; Sela's account.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

changes.why: The fact is about the mine.

properties.details_shown: Morning fog sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere; the party stood at the end of pier four.

sources.quote: The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: GM's description of the docks.

properties.details_shown: Entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted, a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smelling of church and old candle wax. About thirty paces in the tunnel is flooded with warm black water; wet hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.

sources.quote: The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

changes.why: GM's description of the mine and its state.

change.name: Hymn pages in Saltmere signed M. Brand

properties.statement: Hymn-book pages floating in the Saltmere tunnel include one with a hymn about the sea giving back what it takes and "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: A concrete clue found at the mine.

sources.quote: Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Found in the mine.

properties.what_changed: Teo thinks the "M. Brand" page at Saltmere is in Mira's handwriting, so she was there.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

properties.details_shown: At low water only the bell tower and two broken arches stick out of the bay, seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor under the water, like a congregation, until the bell stops and they vanish.
properties.state: Bell rang again at midnight, humming louder.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches.
Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation.

changes.why: GM's description of the chapel and what the party saw.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.
the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder.

changes.why: GM states the clock stands at three of six.

properties.statement: Local fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles.

sources.quote: The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

changes.why: Rumor only, so a world fact and not an NPC.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks, fire going, smells of tar and fish stew.

properties.played_as: Huge man with a red beard, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks; teasing and generous.
